title: Conditioning Large Language Models on Legal Systems? Detecting Punishable Hate Speech
measurement_description: The paper evaluated whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can be conditioned on different levels of legal abstraction to detect punishable hate speech under the German Criminal Code (§ 130). Regarding religion, it specifically measured the models' ability to identify whether hate speech statements targeted a 'religious group' (one of the legally protected categories) and to classify the corresponding criminal conduct, such as incitement to hatred or violation of human dignity.
base_benchmarks: Zufall et al. (2022) legal hate speech dataset
findings: The models performed reasonably well at extracting general target groups (which legally includes religious groups) from text rather than classifying them into predefined categories. However, models struggled significantly to accurately classify the target conduct (e.g., incitement to hatred vs. calling for violence) compared to human legal experts. Models conditioned on abstract legal texts frequently hallucinated and contradicted themselves, demonstrating a lack of deep legal task understanding.
